.. _const-vendor-pairing:

Const-Vendor Pairing
---------------------

**Every module under** :mod:`pcapkit.const` **is generated by a matching crawler
under** :mod:`pcapkit.vendor`, with no exception. A registry copied from an IANA,
IETF or similar web-published table is never hand-maintained -- the crawler
re-scrapes the source and regenerates the module, so a hand edit to the generated
file is silently discarded on the next run. Ruled on :issue:`2495`, which points a
hand-maintained registry at the ``DATA`` attribute below.

The ``DATA`` Attribute, for a Registry With No Web Source
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A source that is not a web-crawlable table does not excuse a module from this
pairing -- it changes what the crawler fetches. :class:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor`
reads its registry two ways: :meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor._request` either
``GET``\ s :attr:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.LINK`, or, when a subclass overrides
:meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.request` to take no arguments, returns a
module-level ``DATA`` literal instead and never touches the network.
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ipx.packet` and :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ipx.socket` are the
precedent: both read a hand-transcribed ``DATA`` dict because their source,
Novell's and Xerox's own IPX socket/packet-type tables, went offline (:issue:`507`,
:issue:`518`).

:class:`~pcapkit.const.linux.arphrd.ARPHRD` follows this pattern: its source is the
Linux kernel header ``<linux/if_arp.h>``, C source under the kernel's own versioning
rather than an IANA page, so :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.linux.arphrd` reads a ``DATA`` dict
of ``{code: (name, description)}`` transcribed from the header. The crawler's
:meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.process` renders that dict into the members, the
``FLAG`` bound and the ``_missing_`` body the committed :mod:`pcapkit.const.linux.arphrd`
carries, so running it is a no-op against the tree, as a web-scraped crawler's run is.
The explanatory prose -- which values are listed and why, the cross-reference to
:class:`~pcapkit.const.arp.hardware.Hardware` -- lives in the crawler's module
docstring and comments, beside the ``DATA`` literal it documents; the generated
``const`` module carries only the templated docstring every generated module does.

Where the primary source is paywalled, a pinned secondary revision is an acceptable
``DATA`` source once its values are cross-checked against independent implementations,
ruled in review of :pr:`2607` (:issue:`2575`). :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ipx` is the earlier
example, and the :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ieee802_11` crawlers check theirs against the
Linux kernel's header and Wireshark.

``LINK``-and-Scrape Pairing: TLS Content Types and HandshakeType
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.content_type.ContentType` and
:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.handshake_type.HandshakeType` have matching crawlers,
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor.tls.content_type` and :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.tls.handshake_type`,
exported as ``TLS_ContentType`` and ``TLS_HandshakeType`` (:issue:`2495`). Both take
the normal ``LINK``-and-scrape shape against IANA's ``tls-parameters-5.csv`` and
``tls-parameters-7.csv``: unlike ARPHRD's, TLS's source is a live, web-published
table, so neither reads a ``DATA`` literal. Running either reproduces its committed
``const`` module byte-for-byte. As for ARPHRD, the protocol-specific prose -- the
record-layer header citations, the Unassigned/Reserved band rationale, the
``_RESERVED``-suffix handling -- lives in the crawlers' module docstrings and
comments.

Lazy Package Imports
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

**A** :mod:`pcapkit.const` **package imports its enumerations on first use**, not with
itself. Ruled by the owner in session and recorded on :issue:`2729`. Its
:file:`__init__.py` names each export in an import under ``if TYPE_CHECKING:``, for
the type checkers, and binds the ``__getattr__`` and ``__dir__`` that
:func:`~pcapkit.utilities.importlib.lazy_exports` returns; :mod:`pcapkit.const` re-exports
its subpackages' ``__all__`` the same way. The one real import is of
:class:`~pcapkit.const.reg.apptype.apptype.AppType` and
:class:`~pcapkit.const.reg.apptype.apptype.TransportProtocol`, which
:mod:`pcapkit.const.reg.apptype` builds
:attr:`AppType.__registries__ <pcapkit.const.reg.apptype.apptype.AppType.__registries__>`
on. A crawler writes the enumeration module and never a package's
:file:`__init__.py`, so regenerating keeps the laziness, and a module a crawler adds
takes its export there by hand, in both places.
:file:`tests/const/test_const_lazy_exports_2729_unit.py` fails on an export imported
outside ``TYPE_CHECKING``, or one that does not resolve to what its import names, and
:file:`tests/const/test_const_apptype_lazy_1538_unit.py` on a package that loads an
enumeration with itself.
